verdictProvider: No subagent judged anything in this round; the tester's own session ran every check, so no provider or model needs naming.

implementerProof.how: Drove the same surface independently at 337c577d on dispatch:local (the head's Go server, Postgres 17, the web app and dispatch CLI built at the head, and the Legion daemon's dispatch.HTTPClient.SetStatus): closes, reopen, upgrade and roll repair, no-op writes, the unloadable-document close, the round-1 red test and offline-edits.e2e.ts.

proof.criterion: Close by a person, an agent session and the Legion daemon withdraws every open ask of every kind and names the closer; answered, retracted and resolved asks stay; blocks and copies read resolved; earlier versions are unchanged and no version is written; the page shows nothing waiting; reopen restores exactly those asks
proof.surface: dispatch:local with the branch's CLI, the daemon's own SetStatus, and Chromium
proof.command: seed.ts TT 3; alice cookie PATCH TT-1; SID=tester-agent-9 dcli issue-update --issue TT-2 --status done; daemonclose TT-3 done; state.ts; look.ts TT-3 (spec and conversation); reopen TT-1 by alice and TT-2 by the agent
proof.observed: Closes took 0.08 and 0.13 s. On each issue open_asks is 0 and the approval draft; d1, p1, p3, h1 and ap read withdrawn by alice | tester-agent-9 | legion-daemon:TT; d2 answered, p2 retracted, p4 resolved; the blocks and the copy read resolved; the latest version is the named pre-close version. In Chromium there is no whose-turn header and no Awaiting approval button, and each card reads 'Withdrawn when legion-daemon:TT closed the issue'. The reopens restored the same 5 ids with the same waiting_on, in the Inbox, approval awaiting, blocks open, and wrote no version.
proof.negativeControl: The same closes on main's build b4bea385 (UP-1..3) left open_asks 5, the approval awaiting and every block open

proof.criterion: Round-3 fixes: a close beside a document that cannot load, a close whose client hangs up, the editor credit across a close and reopen, typing after a read-only-then-writable reconnect
proof.surface: dispatch:local (server API, SQL corruption, curl --max-time) and Dispatch's Playwright harness (chromium and iphone) with a throwaway probe spec
proof.command: Corrupt notes.md's doc_updates of TT-4, restart the server, daemonclose TT-4 done, run repairpass twice; curl --max-time 0.02-0.05 PATCH close on TT-5..9 right after inserting a block; alice edit, then daemon close and agent reopen of TT-1 with version authors read; bun run e2e -- zz-tester-probe.e2e.ts --project chromium --project iphone --repeat-each 2 (deleted after)
proof.observed: TT-4: the notes read gives 409 DOCUMENT_UNLOADABLE; the close returns 200 and withdraws the ask, logging 'leave the ask blocks of a document whose history cannot load as they are'; both repair passes return no error. Each hung-up close (begin, document write, event insert) rolled back whole: the issue stayed in triage, ask and block open, and no room failed. Alice's edit settled as v5 authored by alice before the close, and the close and reopen wrote no version. Probes passed 4 of 4: typing after a writable reconnect was stored and named 'not sent yet', then reached the server; a tab's own unsent typing survived a close and a reopen, then reached the server.
proof.negativeControl: Reading the corrupted document is refused 409 DOCUMENT_UNLOADABLE, so the close really ran beside a document that cannot load
